### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via expandRecipient (symbol, a method of class SharingRuleService))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6af8cf76f92d969649e297be141d21f203f8df6c` — the merge of head `b24881883d2b1704cded17f71731d95b609febee` into base `870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6af8cf76f92d969649e297be141d21f203f8df6c && git checkout 6af8cf76f92d969649e297be141d21f203f8df6c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9 b24881883d2b1704cded17f71731d95b609febee && git checkout -B drift-repro 870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9 && git merge --no-ff b24881883d2b1704cded17f71731d95b609febee

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b24881883d2b1704cded17f71731d95b609febee`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/queue-recipient.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/queue-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/bu-tree-recompute.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/recipient-membership-recompute.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/kernel-queue-membership.ts, packages/objectql/src/assignment-rules.ts, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs, docs/adr/0142-ownership-queue-membership-claim-and-assignment-rules.md (D2, D6, D7 as amended), and for the one red check-run's provenance packages/spec/liveness/query.json and packages/objectql/src/engine.ts

Rendered 2026-11-05T09:23Z. Inputs: card #29604 (body and every comment, the rulings 6594432222, 6599731698 and 6600766777, the route-A ruling 6648946388, the landing note 6652336497 and the part-2 dev report 6653951527 included), PR #30386 (body, eight-path file list, net diff against `main` at the head's merge base `8589756a`, +514/−74), the PR's comments (the seat's claim 6653978618 for this head, the Docs Drift Check), and the check-runs on `b2488188`. The narrowing face: no schema and no governed path in the diff, a `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line in the body and the changeset; the floor is every path outside the prose faces, listed first above, then the files the hunks cite, read at the head (`refs/pm-review/30386-head`, fetched into a ref of my own; nothing checked out, built or run). Part 1 (PR #30288, my records 6650659075 and 6651366716, merged `13c0c5ba`) and the spec slice (#30251, PR #30318) are on the merge base; this is a fresh full record on part 2. CI on the head at posting time: every required context (`Build Core`, `Test Core` 1–8, `Lint & Repo Gates` with every `Lint · *` lane, `TypeScript Type Check` with every `Type Check · *` lane, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`) and `Check Changeset` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` concluded `success`; the UI and opt-in contexts `skipped`; ONE check-run is `failure`, `Spec property liveness`, whose cause is on `main` and not in this diff — ③ states the evidence.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The service's `'refuse'` answer** — `OwnershipQueueService.expandMembers(name, org, { onFailedRead: 'refuse' })` and `isMember(user, name, org, { onFailedRead: 'refuse' })` now reject when the queue's `sys_queue` row (`authoredQueueRow`, its own sentence naming the row read), its `sys_queue_member` walk (`authoredMemberSpecs`, the walk's refusal passed on), a specification's expansion (`expandSpec`: team, position with its `sys_member` limb, the two business-unit kinds) or a holder check (`holderCheck`) fails; the public call wraps once in `queueReadRefusal` (`[queue] queue '…' in organization '…' does not answer its members, because a read behind it failed: …`, the inner read's `[sharing]` tag and "refuses instead" clause cut, the error as `cause`). A narrowing of the service's accept set at the answer the contract declares for exactly this: **right** — ADR-0142 D2 as amended, and the contract's `OwnershipQueueFailedReadAnswer` whose `'refuse'` says "rejects with a failure that names the read, never `[]`, a partial set or `false`". The paged reads already refuse a failed page or an unverifiable walk, so no refusal is an answer on pages already read. An empty queue is `[]` and an unresolved name `[]` / `false` under both answers (pinned).
2. **The default moves nowhere — (a).** Every read keeps its `'nobody'` answer under the default (`expandSpec`, `holderCheck`, `authoredQueueRow`, `authoredMemberSpecs` each guard their throw on `refuse`), and the only non-test callers passing `'refuse'` in the tree are the two D7 sites and the one D6 site. The admission consumers call without it: the sitting-record access path (`sharing-service.ts` :896 `queuesOf`, :952 `isMember`), the claim gate (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` :1602 `isMember`), `explain-access` (:512 `isMember`), the kernel membership read (`kernel-queue-membership.ts` :95 `queuesOf`) and the assignment pool (`assignment-rules.ts` :293 `expandMembers`); `queuesOf`, `queuesNaming` and `hasAnyQueue` take no option at all. **Right**: D3/D4/D5 keep "nobody", as 6594432222 and the brief require. Pinned by the D3 control (team-only member denied, no throw; position member allowed).
3. **D6, the queue arm** — `expandQueueUsers` asks `{ purpose: 'addressing', onFailedRead: 'refuse' }` (:3496); part 1's catch in `resolveApproverSpec` turns the rejection into `ApproverDirectoryUnreadableError` ahead of the "expanded to nobody" return, so the node refuses under every `onEmptyApprovers` policy with the queue's refusal as `failedRead`; pinned per policy with a double that answers as the real service does. The two axes stay independent (`purpose` still `'addressing'`). `decideNode`'s `'literal'` reader meets the same rejection, which its catch records and the queue branch answers with the "could not be expanded" warning and no slot — the slot outcome it had when the service answered nobody. **Right** — D6 as amended; this delivers part 1's "Not yet".
4. **D7, the grant recompute — (b).** `expandRecipient`'s `queue` branch (:2198) and `ruleReachesUser`'s (:1752) pass `'refuse'`. Read in order in the tree: `evaluateResolvedRule` → `desiredGrantsForRule` (:2087 expands after `findMatchingRecords`, before `reconcile`); `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients` reads the existing grants, expands at :1599, and only then diffs and deletes; `reconcileRuleForUser` reads the held grants, asks `ruleReachesUser` at :1679, and only then revokes; `evaluateAllForRecord` expands at :1422 inside the per-rule try before `reconcileForRecord`. So every D7 path throws before any write, and the rule's grants stay. Each production caller isolates the rule and warns: the record pass (:1425) and object pass (:1464), the boot backfill (`sharing-plugin.ts` :237–240), the write-hook reconcile (`scheduleReconcile`, caught and warned in `makeHandler`; the chain's own `.catch` only keeps the chain unpoisoned), `queue-hooks.ts` (:220, :236), `bu-tree-recompute.ts` (:263, :301) and `recipient-membership-recompute.ts` (:319). A direct `evaluateRule` / revoke / per-user call rejects with the service's failure, the answer a `team` or `position` recipient has given since #29503. **Right** — D7 as amended, the #29362 isolation shape; pinned through the real service for both outage tables, the revoke, the per-user pass, the record pass, and convergence after the read returns. An inactive rule still purges without expanding — a deactivation is a decision, not an outage.
5. **`isMember` under `'refuse'` — (c).** `specsReachUser` walks every specification; a successful read that reaches the user answers `true` whichever specification failed; only when none reaches does the first failure become the answer; `false` is never given beside a failure. Against the contract text: "`false` is answered only when every read behind it succeeded" holds exactly; "a failed read rejects with a failure naming it" is read as the case where no successful read reaches the user. **Right in behaviour**: `true` can only keep or create a grant the user is owed (a member by a read that succeeded is a member), never revoke one, so D7's reason for refusing is untouched, and the alternative would make the answer depend on specification order. The contract sentence should say so — ③ carries it. The queue's own `sys_queue` / `sys_queue_member` reads refuse first, before any specification: right, since without them the membership is unknown.
6. **The activation ledger — (d).** `switchedOff` keeps answering "switched on" on a failed read under both answers, logged once; `positionActive` skips the ledger on `'addressing'`, so the D6 slate never consults it, and on D7 (`'access'`) it matches `positionConfersAccess`'s posture for a rule's own position recipient, so a queue's position and a rule's position cannot disagree in one outage. The contract left this to the card; the cost (a D7 pass can grant a switched-off position's holders during a ledger outage) predates the card and is stated. **Right.**
7. **Public surface** — the two service methods now take the options the published contract already declares (merged #30318); `queueReadRefusal`, `WALK_CONSEQUENCE`, `resolve`, `specReachesUser` are module-private; `packages/spec` untouched; `index.ts` of both packages untouched. Nothing published widens. The changeset says so and the gates agree.
8. **Tests** — the new pins are top-level `describe`s in the shared harness files (ruling 6583487846); the D7 pins drive the real `OwnershipQueueService` and `SharingRuleService` over one engine; two existing pins now assert the third argument, so a regression to `'nobody'` at either consumer is red.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29604-queue-service-refuses-failed-read.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`; `!` in the title; a BREAKING banner; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in the PR body and the changeset; one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. No spec key, export or config field moves (the option is the contract's, already published), so the Post-Task Checklist's rule holds: a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition. `Check Changeset` is `success`. **Matches what the diff publishes.**

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — right for the diff: the service's `'refuse'` answer and its two recompute consumers narrow; nothing on a published entry widens.

Judgment (e), part 1's pending entry: its `Clause-②:` sentence ("does not reject yet … until #29604 part 2") and its **Not yet** bullet become false on this merge while both entries are unreleased. The dev first corrected them in place and `check-empty-changeset`'s foreign-changeset rule refused it as designed (a PR may not modify a `.changeset/*.md` on the merge base it did not add); `b2488188` restores the file byte-for-byte from the merge base and the new entry's last bullet names the two sentences and says to read it in their place. As the diff stands this is the only route a seat may take, and `Check Changeset` is green on it. How the published CHANGELOG would read: both are `patch` entries of the same packages in the same release section, so a reader of the whole section reads correctly; a reader who greps `queue` and lands on part 1's entry alone reads "does not reject yet" and is misled — the shape the CHANGELOG guardrail warns of for released entries (a correction elsewhere is one the reader never reaches). ④ should-fix 1 says what is owed before the release consumes the entries.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6653951527: `open_questions: []`. Its stated decisions, each read in the tree: (i) the ledger keeps "switched on" — ① item 6, accepted; (ii) `isMember` answers `true` past a failed specification — ① item 5, accepted in behaviour, contract wording owed; (iii) the queue's own rows refuse first — accepted; (iv) part 1's pending changeset left as on `main`, superseded by name, "needs a person's word, not blocking" — ② (e) and ④ should-fix 1; (v) `Skills-docs:` `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` corrected (part 1's body wrongly said no page stated the failed-read behaviour) — a prose face, not reviewed here; the Docs Drift Check also lists `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` via the `ApprovalService` symbol, and that page names no failed-read or `onEmptyApprovers` behaviour, so no text moves there; (vi) assignee and reviewers unset — the seat's hand-over step.
- Out-of-scope finding, class b: three sentences of the published contract (`OwnershipQueueFailedReadAnswer`: "until then a caller passing `'refuse'` still gets `'nobody'`"; "whether that posture moves is #29604's code half to decide"; `isMember`'s doc not stating `true` past a failure) become stale or incomplete the moment this merges. The dev marks it "carrier: seat · noted, not filed". A contract text that no longer describes the shipped behaviour is a contract defect, which Prime Directive 10 says is filed, not noted — ④ should-fix 2.
- **The red check-run.** `Spec property liveness` (`spec-liveness-check.yml`, triggered here by the `content/docs/**` edit) fails on `query/searchFields → packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`: the liveness entry (`packages/spec/liveness/query.json`, identical on this head and on `origin/main`) cites `engine.ts#expandSearchOnAst` and the key-mention check finds no `searchFields` in that file. This diff touches neither `packages/spec` nor `packages/objectql`. At this PR's head and merge base `engine.ts` names `$searchFields` three times (docblock lines :4898, :4925, :4931); on `origin/main` (`870ebce3`) it names it zero times, because `f672e0dc` (#30341, "move 36 hand-series private docblocks out of engine.ts", on `main` after this PR's merge base) moved those docblocks out. The job checks out the merge of the head into current `main`, which is where the rot appears; nine of the workflow's twelve most recent runs, on unrelated PR and merge-group heads, fail the same way. The context is not among the ten required status checks on `main` (read from the branch rules), so it is advisory. Verdict here: not this PR's; it is `main`'s, the objectql/spec lane's to repoint (the `query/searchFields` evidence to where the docblock now lives), after which a merge of `main` into this branch clears it. The seat applies the main-red convention to the landing.
- Nothing outstanding on this PR; nothing escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

Read against ADR-0142 D2 / D6 / D7 as amended on `main` and the published contract. The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real at every point the spec names: D2's "the consumer says which it is owed when it calls" is the contract's `onFailedRead`; D6's refusal is reached from the real service through part 1's catch; D7's "stop that rule's pass before any revoke, keep the rule's existing grants, log naming the rule and the read" is what each pass does, in that order, with the catches that already isolated a `team` or `position` recipient. No declared capability is taken from a consumer: every admission consumer keeps the answer D2 declares for it, and `queuesOf` (the access path's read) has no refuse axis at all. Tried to break it: a `'refuse'` call cannot answer on a partial set (the memo in `expandSpec` rethrows under refuse, so a later specification cannot mask an earlier failure, and the paged reads refuse rather than truncate); a `'nobody'` call cannot reach `queueReadRefusal` (every throw is guarded on `refuse`, and the outer catch rethrows raw under the default); `isMember`'s `true` past a failure can only keep a grant, never revoke one; the inactive-rule purge in `evaluateResolvedRule` does not expand and so cannot be refused, which is right because deactivation is authored; the write-hook reconcile's chain `.catch` keeps the chain alive while the handler logs the failure; the D6 arm's rejection under the `'literal'` reader lands on the queue branch's failed-read warning and no slot. With part 2 the measured table in 6648911579 (every outage row revoking) is answered: the whole-rule pass, the revoke and the per-user pass now reject before the diff, and the addressing slate refuses the node.

Findings:

- **should-fix 1 — the release must not publish part 1's "does not reject yet" as written (seat, before `changeset version`; not a code change on this head).** Two sentences of the pending `.changeset/29604-approver-directory-refusal-queue-paging.md` are false once this merges, and the correction lives in a different entry. The gate made that a person's decision by design, and the diff takes the only route a seat may. What is owed: the maintainer's word on the dev's three-line in-place correction (or a maintainer-side edit of the pending note at release), so the published `CHANGELOG.md` carries no entry a reader can land on alone and be misled by. Record the decision on the card.
- **should-fix 2 — file the spec-lane follow-up (seat).** The three contract sentences in `packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts` named in ③ describe a state this merge ends; "noted, not filed" leaves the published contract text wrong. File the card (Metadata-protocol none, docblock only, `gen:docs` if the TSDoc is rendered) and link it from #29604 before the card closes on `Fixes`.

No must-fix.
